text:
alex: quick sync — we need a standardized set of per-route/model panels for latency (p50/p95/p99), TTFT (time-to-first-token), and tokens/sec. Goal: consistent panels across hosted/dedicated/private, and filters for model, route, customer_tier, capacity_tier. Runtime needs to emit labels so dashboards can roll up and filter: route, model, batch_size, kvcache, customer_tier, capacity_tier, region, serving_variant. Also would like a fallback_rate metric for routing failovers and an explicit first_token metric.

priya: cardinality question — adding model + route + region + batch will blow up TSDB. Can we emit full labels but rely on recording rules that aggregate? Also who owns the telemetry schema? :thinking:

kevin: agreed re: cardinality. Proposal: runtime emits full label set, but platform defines recording rules for the canonical dashboard series. Keep high-cardinality labels (batch_size, region) for debug-only panels that are sampled. We'll also TTL detailed series faster.

marco: for P95/P99 we should use histograms + histogram_quantile. Example PromQL for P95: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route, customer_tier, capacity_tier))
```
For TTFT the runtime can emit a first-token histogram to avoid stitching. Query example: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_first_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route, customer_tier))
```
Tokens/sec can be derived from a counter: `sum(rate(redwood_tokens_generated_total[1m])) by (model, route)`

jen: Console UX notes — we need a per-route header that shows active model, P95, TTFT, tokens/sec and a quick compare control to compare variants (e.g., quantized vs fp16). Rollout idea: 1) internal preview + feature flag 2) beta on a handful of high-traffic routes 3) lift to all customers. Add a canary panel for fallback_rate to gate the rollout.

alex: ownership idea: eng-runtime owns emission; eng-platform owns recording rules, canonical dashboards and alerting thresholds; devex owns example dashboards and docs; infra/ops reviews retention/cost. Action items:
- alex -> runtime: add labels and emit `redwood_first_token_latency_seconds` histogram + `redwood_tokens_generated_total` counter. Please include `serving_variant` and `kvcache` labels. (due: Fri)
- kevin -> platform: author recording rules to canonicalize p50/p95/p99 and a tokens/sec series; also create reduced-cardinality series for daily dashboards. (due: Mon)
- jen -> console: mockup header + compare UI and canary flow in UI. (due: Wed)
- priya -> infra: sampling plan, retention/cost calc, and spreadsheet sharing. (due: Tue)

kevin: add one more item — quota/throttles need visibility. Suggest we expose `redwood_requests_throttled_total{model,route,customer_tier}` and a panel that overlays throttles on top of latency to spot correlated spikes.

marco: example metric naming + label set we think runtime should emit: 
```
# metric: redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket
# labels: {model, route, customer_tier, capacity_tier, serving_variant, kvcache, batch_size, region}
```
Recommend `route` be the logical route id (not the full URL) and add optional `route_alias` for mapping.

priya: OK — I'll run retention numbers tonight and add a column for estimated cardinality growth if we include region+batch. Will share the sheet. Also +1 on `route_alias` — useful for rollups across variants.

alex: thanks. One UX question: should dashboard defaults show aggregated across regions by default and allow region filter? That keeps the main view low-cardinality. @jen?

jen: yes, default to aggregated (model+route+customer_tier). Add a small dropdown to expand region/batch when needed. Also include an 'explain change' box when switching compare mode (so users know what dimensions differ).

kevin: I'll start the recording-rules PR and include examples for Grafana panels and PromQL recording names like `rwd_p95_request_latency_by_route`. We'll stub the rules with `by (model,route,customer_tier,capacity_tier)`.

alex: can we have a 15m sync tomorrow 10:00 to finalize labeling and ownership? @jen @kevin @priya @marco

deploy-bot: dashboard:eng-platform: preview dashboard 'per-route-latency-throughput' created at https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/per-route-latency-throughput (preview) :eyes:

alex: perfect — thanks everyone, I'll follow up with a single doc that includes the PromQL snippets and the action items.
